audit.whatIsWrong: The two layers disagreed on six of seven rows: full read Pantheon, Pantheon, Pantheon, Pantheon, Skill, Skill, Skill while content win[] and the packet levelChart read Skill, Skill, Skill, Pantheon, Ahri, Ahri, Ahri.
audit.why: Only row 4 matched. The page was telling a paying user that Pantheon wins level 1 in one place and that level 1 is a skill matchup in another, then that level 6 is even in one place and Ahri's in another — with Ahri sitting on a 53.6% win rate over 3280 games, the content layer is the one backed by the data.
audit.corrected: phases[0..2].side to Skill and phases[4..6].side to Ahri, matching win[] on all seven rows; ratings and why text on the flipped rows brought in line.

audit.whatIsWrong: His ultimate was called "Grand Skyfall" in wants.foe[1], and dosFull[2].d cited a "fifteen-second" Shield Vault cooldown.
audit.why: The ultimate is Grand Starfall — 5500 range, 180/165/150 seconds, which is why it is a map tool and not a lane tool. Shield Vault is 13/12/11/10/9, so the fifteen-second figure would have a player step up two full seconds before the stun is actually back.
audit.corrected: Name corrected, cooldown corrected to thirteen seconds, and Grand Starfall's real 180-second rank-1 cooldown added.

audit.whatIsWrong: The decisive interaction in the matchup was absent: Aegis Assault is a channel, and Charm cancels it outright.
audit.why: Riot's E text is a set-shield channel that makes him invulnerable to damage from the front while he strikes. It is 22 seconds at rank 1 — the longest cooldown he has in lane. Ahri's Charm is immobilizing crowd control, so it interrupts the channel instead of being wasted against it, which inverts the standing advice ("waste charm on a shielded window" as a don't). Equally, Shield Vault is a 600-range targeted dash and Charm instantly stops movement abilities, so charm thrown before he commits denies the engage entirely.
audit.corrected: Stated in spikes[1], whys[4], breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0].d and dontsFull[1].d.

audit.whatIsWrong: Mortal Will's empowerment cycle and the Shield Vault auto-attack reset were never mentioned.
audit.why: Every few spells or attacks his next spell is empowered, and his combo opens with an attack reset — the wind-up is the cue to step back, not the ability cast. Without that, a reader watches for the wrong frame.

notes: "Grand Skyfall" corrected to Grand Starfall, and a fabricated fifteen-second Shield Vault cooldown corrected to its real thirteen. The biggest gap was point 4: Aegis Assault is flagged channel in the data AND described by Riot as a set-shield strike sequence, so Charm interrupts it — yet the page listed 'waste charm on a shielded window' as a critical DON'T, which is close to the opposite of the truth. That advice is now inverted with the mechanism stated. Level chart disagreed on six of seven rows; the content layer matched the packet and the win rate, so the full layer was moved to it. Deliberately not asserted: whether Aegis Assault's front-facing invulnerability blocks the orb's true-damage return from behind (Riot says 'from the front' but gives no arc), and whether Charm is cleansable or reduced by tenacity.
